target.title: fix(codex): clean final/yield turn close writes a false "user interrupted" marker into the thread rollout
target.body:
Closes #111019
Related: #109490, #107464, #106961 (progress-reply siblings, fixed by #105365 + #108487 — this PR completes the explicit-final/yield half), #95942 (original stranded-reply bug; its recognition path is untouched), #99442 (adjacent abort-marker *detection*; independent), #92847, #88206 (adjacent open PRs on nearby idle/terminal invariants)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where every cleanly finished codex-runtime turn that ended through the `message` tool's `final:true` (message-tool-only source delivery) or through `sessions_yield` would write Codex's canonical abort marker — *"The user interrupted the previous turn on purpose"* — into the thread rollout, because OpenClaw released the turn via `turn/interrupt`. Subsequent turns on that thread start from context falsely claiming the user aborted, and any work genuinely still running on the turn was killed at the moment the final reply delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The interrupt was never what ended the turn — turn completion and resolution are OpenClaw-side bookkeeping on the lines right after it; the RPC only stopped the Codex child from generating, at the cost of a permanent false marker in Codex's canonical thread state that OpenClaw cannot rewrite.

The shipped solution treats a successful terminal tool result as **"delivery final"**: the attempt stays subscribed and lets the turn end through Codex's own `turn/completed` (the existing terminal-notification path), so the rollout stays clean in the normal case where the model wraps within seconds of its declared final. A dedicated **absolute 10s deadline** — deliberately not activity-resetting, so post-final generation cannot extend it — falls back to the existing interrupt for runaway turns, as does a new inbound user message (the user's next turn never waits out the window). The fallback records its cause (`turn.terminal_release_interrupt`, set before the RPC) so terminal classification treats it as an OpenClaw-initiated clean release: it is not counted as a user abort, and it does not demote a turn whose reply was already delivered into a failed attempt (which would otherwise trigger failure handling/retries for a success).

Boundaries: no app-server protocol changes, no new config surface, no changes to other runtimes (`final` remains Codex-only), and the #95942 recognition path (delivered source replies suppressing the stranded-reply fallback) is untouched. In the fallback case Codex still writes its marker — the protocol has no graceful-stop verb (only `turn/interrupt` / `turn/steer`) and the marker text is fixed on Codex's side, so that residual is an upstream Codex (OpenAI) limitation, tracked as alternative C in #111019.

**Product direction welcome:** the defaults here — 10s deadline value, post-final output appended through the normal projector/mirror path, new-inbound-interrupts-immediately policy — are proposals, laid out with alternatives in #111019. If maintainers prefer different explicit-final semantics, the clean-close path and the fallback policy are separable seams and I'm happy to reshape.

## User Impact

Codex-runtime agents that reply via the message tool (or yield to subagents) no longer accumulate false "user interrupted" context in their native thread history — model behavior on long-lived threads stops degrading toward "the user keeps aborting me". Work still in flight when the final reply delivers is no longer silently killed; it gets up to 10s to finish naturally. In the unexpected-runoff case, turn bookkeeping (e.g. typing indicator) can persist up to those 10s after the final reply — the reply delivery itself is not delayed.

## Evidence

- **Before (production 2026.7.1, codex runtime, message-tool-only):** codex session rollouts accumulate one `turn_aborted` / "user interrupted the previous turn on purpose" entry per ordinary clean close; provenance and file-level analysis in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/109490#issuecomment-5007893467.
- **Focused tests (15 new):** `run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.test.ts` — clean close arms the deadline and does not interrupt/resolve; failed sends keep steering open (negative path, unchanged); repeat release is a no-op; deadline interrupt fires exactly once with attribution set before the RPC; new-inbound interrupt wins over the deadline exactly once; no interrupt once completed; a genuine user abort is never re-attributed as a clean release; no release before a terminal result. `attempt-turn-watches.test.ts` — deadline is absolute (activity does not reschedule it), fires once, skipped after completion/abort, cleared explicitly and via `clearAllTimers`.
- **Extension lane:** `pnpm test:extension codex` — 2643/2643 passing on the rebased branch.
- **Typecheck:** `check:changed` local lanes green including `typecheck extensions` and `typecheck extension tests`; extension typecheck error delta vs base is zero.
- **Sibling/regression notes:** the closest sibling release path (assistant-completion idle recovery watch) is explicitly disarmed while a terminal release is pending so the two release owners cannot race; the steering fence at terminal classification is retained so accepted steers are never dropped by a later fallback interrupt.
- **Live app-server after-fix proof (real Codex app-server, patched branch):** added a repo-conventional live lane, `run-attempt-final-close.live.test.ts` (gated behind `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1` + `OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_FINAL_CLOSE=1` + `OPENAI_API_KEY`), that drives the full run-attempt pipeline — real spawned app-server process, real model turns, real dynamic `message` tool with the injected `final` control — for all three close paths. 3/3 passing; full redacted traces (JSON-RPC timeline, `turn/completed` statuses, rollout marker scan) in the evidence comment below. Headline numbers:
  - *Clean `final:true` close:* zero `turn/interrupt` RPCs, natural `turn/completed` (`status: "completed"`) ~1.6–3.5s after the final tool return, rollout contains **0** abort markers.
  - *Forced post-final runaway* (model instructed to start a ~30s tool after its final reply): exactly one `turn/interrupt`, fired **10.1s** after the final tool return (the absolute deadline), turn ends `interrupted`, attempt result stays successful with no prompt error — the delivered reply is never demoted.
  - *New inbound during the grace window* (queued 2s after the final reply): `turn/interrupt` fired **~0.1s** after the queue (2.1s after final), i.e. the follow-up never waits out the deadline.
- **Residual found and fixed by the live proof (second commit):** with the interrupt no longer classified as a user abort, a deadline-killed in-flight tool call surfaced its unmatched `tool.call` as a missing-tool-result **prompt error**, failing an attempt whose reply was already delivered. The event projector now marks OpenClaw-initiated terminal-release closes and skips the prompt-error escalation for exactly that case (killed tool calls still record failed tool results for audit consumers); covered by a new `event-projector.test.ts` case plus the pre-existing fail-closed control case, and re-verified live (runaway scenario now closes with no prompt error).

Release-note context: fix — codex app-server turns that end via message `final:true` or `sessions_yield` now finish through Codex's own `turn/completed` instead of `turn/interrupt`, so clean closes no longer write a false "user interrupted" marker into the thread rollout (bounded by a 10s fallback). Surface: codex runtime turn lifecycle. Refs: #111019, #109490, #105365, #108487.

**Merge-risk (session-state):** the changed surface is the codex attempt's own release/terminal path; cross-session state is untouched. The riskiest interaction — resolution now depending on the terminal notification — is backstopped by the existing completion-idle (60s), attempt-idle, and terminal-idle watches, which remain armed through the window and still abort/resolve a wedged turn exactly as before. Race coverage: exactly-once transition tests above; genuine aborts cancel the deadline via the shared abort signal guard.

AI assistance disclosure: implemented and tested by an AI agent (Claude) operated by @JP0P / @clawSean, with human review of design decisions and this description. Maintainer edits are enabled.
